intro: Where are you right now? In a room. In a building. On a street. In a city or a town. In the state of Illinois. In the United States. On planet Earth. A map can show every one of those places.

In this unit you will learn to read a map and to make one. You will learn the four directions. You will find Chicago and Illinois on a globe. Then you will look at the land and water around you: hills, plains, rivers and one very big lake.
You will also see how weather changes what we wear and do. You will see how people change places, and how places change people. And you will learn ways to take care of the place where you live.
bigQuestion: How do maps and places help us understand where we live?

timeline.t: The class hides a treasure and draws a map of the room from above.
The class adds a key: a star means treasure, a square means desk.
The class walks the halls and draws a map of the whole school.
Everyone finds north by watching where the sun comes up.
The class spins a globe and finds the United States, Illinois and Chicago.
Nia's family drives south from Chicago and watches the land go flat.
At the farm, Nia sees fields of corn where prairie grass once grew.
The weather turns cold. Coats and mittens come out of the closet.
The class picks up litter in the park and plants a tree.

words.d: a drawing of a place as seen from above
the list on a map that tells what each symbol means
the direction at the top of most maps
the path you take from one place to another
a big piece of flat land
water with land all around it
one of the four parts of the year: winter, spring, summer, fall

test.q: A map shows a place the way who sees it?
test.why: A map is a drawing of a place from above, like a bird's view.

test.q: On the class treasure map, what stood for treasure?
test.why: The key said: star means treasure. Square meant desk.

test.q: On most maps, north is at the…
test.why: On most maps, north is at the top and south is at the bottom.

test.q: On a globe, most of Earth is what color?
test.why: There is more water than land on Earth, so most of a globe is blue.
Chicago is a city inside Illinois. Illinois is a state inside the United States.

test.q: Which is water that flows in a long, thin path?
test.why: A river flows from high land to low land in a long, thin path.
Illinois is mostly flat. It was prairie and is now mostly farmland.

test.q: What do people in Chicago wear in January?
test.why: January in Chicago is cold and snowy, so people dress warm.

test.q: Which shows a place shaping people?
choices: A town by the sea has many fishers
test.why: The sea is right there, so people become fishers. The place shaped their jobs.

test.q: Why should we keep trash out of Lake Michigan?
test.why: Lake Michigan gives Chicago its drinking water. Clean water is for everyone.

write.prompt: Draw a map of the route from your classroom door to one place in your school. Then write: My map helps a new student because... Use the key, a direction word and one thing they pass.
tips: Say what your map helps someone do. That is your claim.
Point to your key and your symbols. That is your evidence.
Tell how the symbols and directions get the new student there. That is your reasoning.
Ask a friend to try your map. If they get lost, fix the map.
